close_reason: Doc-only fixes: updated stale/ambiguous rustdoc and CHANGELOG entries
description:
Scenario: caller writes 'if let AiaError::UriUnsupported(scheme) = e { metrics::inc("aia.unsupported.".to_string() + &scheme); }' expecting the payload to be the URI scheme.

Maintenance consequence: pkix-aia/src/lib.rs:171-178 says: 'The inner String is typically the offending URI or its scheme (e.g. "ldap://example.com/cn=ca" or "ldap").' That is two distinct shapes — a full URI vs just the scheme — and the wording 'typically … or' explicitly accepts both. Downstream consumers cannot reliably split on '://', cannot reliably URL-parse, cannot reliably build metrics keys.

Worse, two adapters can both emit UriUnsupported with different conventions, and the consumer cannot tell which one produced which. The serde-friendly Eq invariant (non-negotiable #6) means cache replay sees these as distinct, so the same upstream condition can produce two cache entries.

Fix options:
(a) Pick scheme-only. Adapters strip to the scheme before constructing UriUnsupported. Easy to consume; loses the URI for logging (but the chain-build layer typically has the URI elsewhere).
(b) Pick full URI. Adapters MUST pass the entire URI through. Consumers parse out the scheme.
(c) Split into two variants: UriSchemeUnsupported(String) and UriMalformed(String). More precise; expands the surface.

Picking either (a) or (b) is a doc fix plus an adapter contract note. The current text invites the divergence; this needs to be tight before pkix-aia-http and any future adapters land.

The existing test at lines 853-861 happens to use the full URI ('ldap://ca.example/cn=ca'). That is the test, not the contract. The contract is the rustdoc.
title: UriUnsupported(String) payload semantics undefined: scheme vs full URI
